title: I Logged Out of the Shared Netflix After the Breakup Like an Adult

parts.text: I changed the streaming password and felt both petty and correct. I am twenty-six, kitchen-table designer, leftover profile named Evan. The relationship ended on a Saturday. The profile lived until Tuesday, because I am tired, not because I was bait. He used it to watch a show we had started, which felt like someone eating my leftovers in a ghost kitchen. The TV still had a smudge from his hair product on the remote, specific, vanilla-ish. I wiped it. I emailed the new password to no one. He texted that I was small. I said the bill was in my name. Small is a $16.99 line item I will not fund as alimony. I watched the show alone and did not enjoy it, which is also allowed. The remote still gets dusty. I did not smash anything. That is my nuclear, apparently: a password and a wipe. I can live with small. I could not live with his profile staring from the row like a roommate. Evan said, "You're being small" I said, "The bill is in my name" My sister said I should have left it to look unevolved. I said I prefer evolved and cheap. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened.

social.video_title: I cut the shared streaming and wiped the vanilla remote
social.description: $16.99 is not alimony. The leftover profile had to go. Would you have waited longer than Tuesday?
